svg.title: Figure 3 — The three tiers of the Axiom store
svg.desc: Three columns side by side. Tier one is the materialised TBox triple array, a few thousand entries of subject, predicate and object. Tier two is the flattened restriction triple array built by buildRBox, holding only some- and value-restrictions. Tier three is the compact individual record array with its three indexes: indIndex by IRI, byType by class, and byCustomer built lazily and stamped with the store version. Each tier is annotated with its size characteristic and the reason it is stored that way.
svg.text: FIGURE 3
Store structure — three tiers, three different bargains
One store object, three storage strategies. Each tier is shaped by how it is read, not by how it was authored.
TIER 1 · MATERIALISED
TBox triples
store.tbox : Array<[s, p, o]>
Written once by buildTBox(). o is an IRI string, or a
literal object { lit, dt } produced by lit().
SUBJECT · PREDICATE · OBJECT
pizza:Pizza rdfs:subClassOf pizza:Food
pizza:Pizza rdf:type owl:Class
pizza:hasTopping rdfs:domain pizza:Pizza
pizza:Margherita rdfs:label "Margherita"
… one entry per asserted TBox axiom
SIZE CHARACTERISTIC
Bounded and small. It tracks the number of authored
axioms, not the data: a few thousand entries, stable
across every dataset size the Dataset menu offers.
store.tbox.length is the first term of tripleCount().
WHY IT IS STORED THIS WAY
The TBox is authored, small, and read in every
direction — subject-bound, predicate-bound, object-
bound and wholly unbound. No single index would
serve all four, and at this size none needs to: a
linear array walk is already fast enough, and it keeps
scan() honest — one code path, no special cases.
Materialising also makes the TBox the one tier that
can be serialised straight back out to OWL.
COST OF THE CHOICE
Every scan touches every TBox triple. Acceptable only
because the array cannot grow with the dataset.
TIER 2 · FLATTENED
Restriction triples
store.rbox : Array<[s, p, o]>
Derived by buildRBox() from entity restrictions and
equivalents. Never authored, never serialised.
SOURCE AXIOM
pizza:Margherita ⊑
hasTopping some MozzarellaTopping
buildRBox()
FLATTENED TRIPLE
pizza:Margherita pizza:hasTopping
pizza:MozzarellaTopping
SIZE CHARACTERISTIC
Smallest tier. One entry per some- or value-restriction
target — hundreds, not thousands. Only q === 'some'
and q === 'value' are flattened.
only · max · exactly · not are deliberately excluded.
WHY IT IS STORED THIS WAY
In OWL an existential restriction is a blank-node class
expression, so a naive triple store would force every
query to walk owl:Restriction, owl:onProperty and
owl:someValuesFrom to answer one question. Flattening
it to a direct subject-predicate-object row lets the
console express the useful query in one pattern.
It is kept apart from store.tbox because it is derived:
rebuild it, never edit it, never export it as asserted.
COST OF THE CHOICE
The flattening is lossy — cardinality and universal
restrictions are invisible to a query over this tier.
TIER 3 · COMPACT RECORDS
Individual records + indexes
store.inds : Array<Record>
Ten scalar fields per individual. No triple object is
ever allocated for an individual, at any dataset size.
RECORD SHAPE
{ i, iri, type, typeName, ref,
branch, price, ts, rating, cust }
cust is an integer offset into store.customers
INDEXES OVER THE SAME ARRAY
indIndex iri→rec
byType cls→rec[]
byCustomer cust→rec[] lazy, version-stamped
SIZE CHARACTERISTIC
Linear in the individual count and nothing else. Seven
triples per pizza and two per customer are counted by
tripleCount(), never materialised.
100,000 pizzas ⇒ 766,000 triples reported, 0 allocated.
WHY IT IS STORED THIS WAY
A triple array for the ABox would cost seven objects
and seven strings per individual, and would still need
the same indexes on top. The record array gives the
table its rows directly, gives scan() its bindings
through DEMO_PRED accessor functions, and gives
neighboursOf() its instance lists through byType.
byCustomer is rebuilt only when store.version moves,
so an edit invalidates it without an explicit flush.
COST OF THE CHOICE
Only the predicates named in DEMO_PRED exist for the
ABox. The record shape is the ABox schema.
REPORTED STORE SIZE
tripleCount() = store.tbox.length + store.inds.length * 7 + store.customers.length * 2 // rbox is derived, so it is not counted
Figure 3 · Store tiers. Illustrates 11-data-model-and-store.md, “Three tiers” and “Why the ABox is not triples”. [src: buildTBox(), buildRBox(), generateIndividuals(), tripleCount()]
